list: The published PS5 list: 55 trophies in total — 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver and 46 bronze.
sources: Exophase trophy list for Grand Theft Auto VI (PSN): https://www.exophase.com/game/grand-theft-auto-vi-psn/trophies/
PSNProfiles trophy page for Grand Theft Auto VI: https://psnprofiles.com/trophies/43531-grand-theft-auto-vi
PlayStation Network — the official names, descriptions and grades reproduced from PSN

roadmap.title: Opening hours — Chapter 1 without rushing
roadmap.text: Begin the campaign and play through Gone Fishing, Breakfast Run and the rest of Chapter 1. Two habits start here and pay off for the whole run: keep a fresh manual save before each chapter closes, and feed the long counters whenever the game hands you a chance — hop into unfamiliar vehicles, take stunt jumps you pass, and actually spend shop money instead of sitting on it.

roadmap.title: Chapters 2 to 4 — story beats and one-off moments
roadmap.text: Work the story through Chapters 2, 3 and 4 plus the named missions The Cartel Heist, Child's Play, Headliners, VCIA Takedown and Operation Savage Glory. Some places and scenes may not be freely reachable later, so handle their moment trophies on the spot: an unscheduled way out of VCIA, a cocktail moment on Ocean Beach, and a loud exit from a vehicle showroom. The missable flags in this guide exist because of descriptions like these.

roadmap.title: Strangers — finish strands, do not just start them
roadmap.text: Take stranger strands as they appear and close each one out: the finales for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone, the unique-animal job for Bret, and eight completed strands in total for the silver Strangers & Freaks. A strand only counts when its final mission is done, so one finished strand beats three half-finished ones.

roadmap.title: Activities — sample everything, then chase the scores
roadmap.text: First pass: try all nine activity types once for Master of None. Second pass: the scored work — gold medals across all 42 Shooting Range challenges, a Top Fun drone win at each of the 14 locations, 20 wins in different races, a fishing win over Cal, one arcade game played to the end, and the bowling follow-through at Kolt & Associates. All of it is repeatable, so this stage costs time, never trophies.

roadmap.title: The long haul — collectibles and big counters
roadmap.text: The largest block of the platinum. Clear Leonida district by district so the sweeps overlap: meditate at all 18 spots, finish 3 Collectible Card sets, WAiNK It at 100 locations, discover 100 vehicles, open up all 52 areas, complete 50 Challenges and land 250 stunts. Keep the counters in this tracker updated as you travel; these trophies punish late starts, not mistakes.

roadmap.title: Crime, partners and the money loop
roadmap.text: With money and gear in place, clear the crime set: 5 Bank Vault robberies with escapes, an Armored Truck job, one Illegal Operation per gang for all 9 gangs, an undetected jewelry store robbery, and the two partner jobs — shaking a 4-star Wanted Level together, and robbing 3 shops in a row together without the heat dropping. Then close the cash loop: launder $250,000 in Marked Bills, spend $100,000 in shops, buy all 8 garage properties and register 10 vehicles on the Scooter Bros app.

roadmap.title: Endgame — cleanup, 100 percent, finale, platinum
roadmap.text: Use the tracker filters to sweep what remains. Start with anything missable-flagged; if a moment was walked past, reload one of the rotating saves from Stages 1 and 2. Then clear the vague one-offs — the partnership moment, the fail-then-succeed moment and the strange event — and push the completion counter to 100 percent for A Long Road. Save the final mission for last so the story trophies land together, and Vice Got a Price! follows automatically once the other 54 are earned. The 90–130 hour total is an estimate derived from the official counts (250 stunts, 100 WAiNK spots, 42 range golds, 52 areas), not a guarantee.
trophies: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the platinum, and it needs no action of its own: earn the other 54 trophies and it unlocks on its own. Plan backwards from it — take the missable moments during the story (roadmap Stages 1 and 2), keep the big counters ticking from the opening hour, and hold 100 percent completion and the final mission for the end. Name, description and grade are PlayStation's, via Exophase and PSNProfiles; the planning advice is written for this guide.
steps: Earn each of the other 54 trophies
Use the progress header to spot what is left
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, through to its finish. It is the first mission of the campaign, so anyone starting the story will reach it immediately; there is no extra condition attached. Description taken from PlayStation via Exophase and PSNProfiles; the how-to here is our own summary of it.
steps: Reach the end of the mission
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every mission grouped under Chapter 1 and the trophy lands as the chapter ends. Stick to the main story markers for now and leave side content for later, but do save manually near the chapter's end — the Stage 1 habit that protects one-off moments inside the chapter.
steps: Keep a manual save near the finale
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2. The asterisks in the name are PlayStation's own spelling, reproduced exactly as published, not a censor applied by this guide. The description adds no side condition, so story progress alone earns it.
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3. As with the other chapter trophies there is no hidden extra requirement in the official wording. Use the driving between missions productively — vehicle discoveries and stunt jumps both feed counters you will want finished later.
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4. By the end of this chapter the map and most side systems should be open, which is exactly why the roadmap puts the stranger and activity sweeps immediately after it. Close the chapter first, then branch out.
steps: Finish the chapter finale, then start the side sweeps
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission — one of only two golds on the list. The roadmap deliberately holds it for Stage 7, because the official wording makes no promise about what remains available after the ending. Clear collectibles, activities and the 100 percent push first if you want a tidy finish, and keep a save from before the finale either way.
steps: Complete it to earn the gold
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Finish the named early-story mission Breakfast Run. Mission-name trophies like this one are earned simply by completing that mission, and following the Chapter 1 markers brings you to it naturally.
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Finish the named mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions usually include their own setup steps, so work through those rather than rushing the finale, and save beforehand in case a partner moment shares the same window.
steps: Unlock The Cartel Heist in the story
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Finish the named mission Child's Play in normal story flow. The official description states no extra condition, so completing the mission is the entire requirement.
steps: Reach Child's Play in the story
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Finish the named mission Headliners when the story offers it. The all-caps styling of the trophy name is PlayStation's and is kept as published.
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Finish the named mission VCIA Takedown. The same airport hosts Catch Me If You Can, the unscheduled-departure trophy, so do not leave the area the second this mission ends — check that entry and use the visit. That pairing is this guide's inference from the two official descriptions, and it is labelled as inference.
steps: Reach VCIA Takedown in the story
While at VCIA, attempt Catch Me If You Can
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Finish the named mission Operation Savage Glory in story flow. No side condition is stated in the official description.
steps: Reach Operation Savage Glory in the story
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100 percent game completion — the list's second gold and the natural end of the roadmap. Trust the in-game percentage as the source of truth and use this tracker to find what feeds it. If the number stalls in the high nineties, the cause is usually a whole category you have barely touched — story, strangers, activities, collectibles or exploration — so audit category by category with the kind filter instead of wandering.
steps: Clear any category you have skipped
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Land 250 stunts for this silver. It is a volume trophy, not a skill trophy: the reliable method is to start in Stage 1 and take every ramp and jump your travel passes, rather than saving all 250 for one endgame grind. Keep the running total in this tracker's counter so the final stretch is a plan, not a guess.
steps: Log the count in this app
Sweep the remainder area by area
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample each activity type once — nine types in the official list data. Winning is not required, only trying, which makes this the ideal first pass before the scored activity trophies in Stage 4. Tick each type in the counter as you go so none is quietly skipped.
steps: Try each of the 9 types once
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Score gold in all 42 Shooting Range challenges for this silver. Treat it as practice: learn one weapon category at a time, replay a challenge immediately while its layout is fresh, and only move on once it is gold so silvers never pile up behind you. Fully repeatable and not missable — patience is the only cost.
steps: Replay each one until it scores gold
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location — 14 locations in the official list data. Only a win at a new location moves the counter; repeating a favourite course does not. Work the map as a circuit, scout each course with one run, then take the win on the next run while the line is still fresh.
steps: Win it, then move to the next of the 14
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The word different does the work in the official wording: twenty wins on one easy circuit will not finish it. Spread wins across the race list, and pair the effort with Top Fun in Stage 4 so the same driving feeds two trophies.
steps: Log distinct wins in the counter
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in his fishing challenge. Use a first attempt to learn how the challenge scores, then replay straight away for the win — challenges like this are repeatable, so a loss costs only a retry. If fishing controls are new to you, practise in free fishing first so the challenge attempt is not also your tutorial. This entry names no spot or bait the official description does not name.
steps: Learn the scoring on a first attempt
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Finish one arcade game — played through to its actual end, per the official wording, not abandoned at a good score. Pick the shortest cabinet you find and this should be among the quickest bronzes on the list.
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Andy's stranger strand. Strands are chains, so work Andy's earlier missions as they appear and the finale will unlock; expecting the last mission first does not work. Finishing strands also builds toward the silver Strangers & Freaks, which needs eight.
steps: Start Andy's strand when it appears
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Kenton's stranger strand, after working the strand's earlier missions as they appear on the map. Counts toward the eight strands required for Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Billy's stranger strand, after finishing the strand's earlier missions. Counts toward the eight strands required for Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete eight full stranger mission strands across Leonida for this silver. It sits on top of the individual finale bronzes for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and others. The classic trap is eight strands started and none finished: pick one strand, close it, then move on. The counter in this tracker exists for exactly that bookkeeping.
steps: Finish strands one at a time
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Randy's stranger strand, after its earlier missions. Counts toward the eight strands required for Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Tyrone's stranger strand, after its earlier missions. Counts toward the eight strands required for Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida — 18 spots in the official list data. Treat it as a collectible sweep: clear spots region by region alongside the exploration trophy The Goodtime State, and log each spot, because quiet locations are very easy to miscount at seventeen of eighteen.
steps: Find meditation spots region by region
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal for Bret, as the official description puts it. Work Bret's strand until the hunt is offered, then prepare before engaging — a unique target is the last thing you want to fumble and have to re-trigger. No species or location is invented here, because the official wording names none.
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete three full Collectible Card sets for this silver. It rewards finished sets, not raw card totals, so chase the cards that close a nearly-complete set before scattering effort into a new one, and log sets rather than loose cards in the counter.
steps: Collect with set completion in mind
Close one full set at a time
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 locations for this silver. Like the stunts, it rewards an early start: WAiNK at new locations as story and exploration uncover them, keep the total logged, and leave only the remainder for a district-by-district endgame sweep alongside The Goodtime State's 52 areas.
steps: WAiNK It at new locations as you find them
Sweep the remainder by district to 100
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 Challenges. Challenges accumulate across almost everything else on this list, so check your existing total before grinding anything specific — races, range work and exploration may already cover a large share. Spend deliberate effort only on the remainder, picking the shortest challenges left.
steps: Check your existing challenge total first
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner alongside you, build a 4-star Wanted Level and then shake it completely. The trophy lives in the escape, not the crime, so set it up on purpose: raise the level together, keep a getaway vehicle ready, break line of sight and keep moving until every star clears with your partner still present.
steps: Break away and lose the level entirely
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in a row with your partner while keeping your Wanted Level alive the whole time — the mirror image of Hot Together, where the heat must never fully drop. Choose three nearby shops before starting, rob the first, and drive straight to the next without hiding long enough to clear your stars. Planning the little circuit first is most of the work.
steps: Pick 3 nearby shops with your partner
Rob them as one unbroken chain
Never let the Wanted Level fully clear mid-chain
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Variety over time is what pays: get into unfamiliar vehicles whenever you spot one parked or in traffic, especially when a new district brings new traffic with it. Started in Stage 1 this nearly finishes itself; started at the end it becomes a car-park crawl. Log discoveries in the counter.
steps: Enter unfamiliar vehicles as you pass them
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Drop five enemies inside a single Combat Focus activation. Do not spend the ability on scattered targets: wait until five or more enemies are in view, line up the easiest ones first, then trigger it and work through the group before it ends. A failed attempt costs nothing — reposition and wait for the next cluster.
steps: Find a group of 5 or more enemies
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE. The official wording describes one specific act at one named place — an unscheduled departure from VCIA, the airport that also hosts the VCIA Takedown mission. Advice drawn from that wording alone: while a mission or free access has you at VCIA, leave by air in a way no timetable would approve of, and do it during the VCIA story window in Stage 2 with a save kept from beforehand, because this guide cannot promise the same opening returns later. The missable flag and method are this guide's inference from the description, labelled as inference.
steps: Keep a save before the VCIA story window
While at VCIA, depart in an unscheduled way
If it does not trigger, reload and try another departure
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The official description is a joke rather than an instruction — it only says things get hot in Rhinos, the tank class of vehicle. Honest reading from that alone: this concerns Rhinos, so when the story or a high wanted level puts you in or against one, engage with it instead of fleeing, and save first because a tank encounter can end a session fast. No exact trigger is invented here, because PlayStation's published wording states none.
steps: Interact with the Rhino instead of fleeing
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without ever being detected — a quiet job, the opposite of the loud partner robberies. Go in low-key, avoid drawing attention inside, and leave without a detection state triggering. If you are spotted, walk away and reset rather than finishing loudly, because a detected robbery cannot count here.
steps: Leave clean — reset and retry if spotted
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five Bank Vaults and escape after each one, for this silver. Note the official wording: a robbery only counts together with its escape, so a vault you are caught leaving is practice, not progress. Build one repeatable loop — enter, clear the vault, leave on a prepared vehicle, lose the heat — run it five times, and log each clean escape.
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an Armored Truck and escape. When you spot one, the job has two halves and only the second pays: take its cargo, then switch immediately to escape driving instead of fighting the response. Prepare the getaway before you open the truck up.
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — 52 areas in the official list data. Exploration overlaps with nearly everything else, so route collectible sweeps (meditation spots, WAiNK locations, cards) through districts you have not opened yet, and check the counter after each trip so the final missing area becomes a deliberate visit rather than a mystery.
steps: Travel through new districts as you play
Route collectible sweeps through unexplored areas
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang — nine gangs in the official list data, one operation per gang being enough, so breadth beats depth. The trap is hitting the same convenient gang repeatedly; log which gangs you have covered and deliberately pick a new gang's operation each time. No gang is named here that the official list does not name.
steps: Identify which gang owns an Illegal Operation
Repeat until all 9 gangs are covered
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE. The official wording describes a single leisure moment at a named place: a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Take it the first time the game gives you quiet time around Ocean Beach instead of assuming a story scene will hand it to you later — keep it in mind during early Vice City time, in Stages 1 and 2. Name, ellipsis and description are reproduced exactly as PlayStation publishes them; the missable flag is this guide's caution from the one-moment shape of the wording.
steps: Go to Ocean Beach when you have free time there
Enjoy a cocktail with a view
Do it early rather than leaving it to cleanup
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE. The official wording describes a specific stunt in a specific kind of place: leaving a vehicle showroom by smashing out of it in a vehicle, through the frontage rather than a door. If a mission or a showroom visit puts you inside with a car, take the loud exit then and there, in Stage 2, and keep a save from before showroom story beats. The flag is this guide's inference from that one-scene description.
steps: Keep a save before showroom story moments
Get into a vehicle inside a showroom
Drive out through the showroom frontage
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: The official wording points at one named venue — the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley — and at a follow-through there. Go to that alley, bowl, and complete the action the description hints at, a proper follow-through on your delivery, rather than merely visiting the building. Trophy name and description, curly apostrophe included, are exactly as PlayStation publishes them.
steps: Visit the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: MISSABLE, flagged openly: the official wording — a partnership with mass appeal — is deliberately vague and names no place, count or action, so no honest guide can hand you a verified step for it yet. What the list itself supports: it sits among the partner trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy), so do partner activities thoroughly, take partner set-pieces when offered, and keep rotating saves through the story so a one-off partnership moment can be replayed. Nothing beyond what the description supports is claimed here.
steps: Complete the other partner trophies thoroughly
Take partner moments when the story offers them
Keep rotating saves through the story
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: MISSABLE-ADJACENT, flagged because its subject is choices, and choices cannot all be revisited within one playthrough. The official wording says only that choices are made, for better or worse, while the official list data carries a PSN count of 500 for it — so treat it as a volume-of-decisions trophy: make choices actively whenever the game offers them (dialogue, mission and world decisions) instead of defaulting past them, and track progress against the 500 target. If a branch ever locks content, the rotating Stage 1 saves are your insurance.
steps: Track progress toward the 500 PSN target
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: MISSABLE. The official wording describes succeeding after a first failure — a shape a flawless first-try playthrough could walk straight past. Method drawn from that wording alone: when an attempt fails naturally, retry it immediately instead of reloading to erase the failure, because a fail-then-succeed sequence is exactly what the phrasing rewards. If you reach the end of the story without it, deliberately fail a repeatable attempt once and then succeed on the second try. This is a reading of the wording, labelled as a reading, not a confirmed trigger.
steps: Do not reload away natural failures
If needed, fail a repeatable attempt once, then succeed
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: MISSABLE. The official wording is the classic shape of a strange, possibly random world event — something witnessed rather than scheduled. The practical advice that follows from that shape alone: explore on foot and at odd hours as well as by highway, avoid fast-travelling past the world, and when something odd starts happening, stay and watch it finish instead of driving on. No event, place or creature is invented here, because the official wording names none.
steps: Explore the world instead of only fast-travelling
Investigate anything strange instead of driving past
Watch the event through to its end

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock a target down with a melee drive-by, per the official wording — striking from a moving vehicle with melee, not with the vehicle itself and not with a firearm. Set it up at low speed on a quiet street so the swing connects cleanly: roll past the target and strike as you pass. It is repeatable in free roam, so a miss costs only another pass.
steps: Prepare a melee option for drive-by use
Strike with melee as you pass

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts — a money-loop trophy with a large round target in the official wording. Build the loop by Stage 6 at the latest: whenever Marked Bills reach you, route them through contacts instead of sitting on them, and log the laundered total so the last stretch is a planned set of runs. Pair it with Treat Yo Self, since a healthy money loop feeds both laundering and spending.
steps: Unlock contacts who launder Marked Bills
Route Marked Bills through them regularly
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. The official phrasing means cumulative shopping, not one giant purchase. Spend from Stage 1 onward — vehicles, clothes, services and upgrades you actually want — instead of hoarding cash for a single endgame splurge, and this bronze typically lands on its own during Stage 6 property buying.
steps: Spend normally in shops from early on
Avoid hoarding all cash to the end
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy all garage properties — eight in the official list data. This is a cash gate, not a skill gate: it waits on the money loop of robberies, laundering and story paydays, so schedule it in Stage 6 once income is steady, buy garages as they become affordable rather than in one sitting, and log each purchase. The garages also give your vehicle collecting a home, which supports Whip It Good habits.
steps: Buy each garage as it becomes affordable
trophies.sources: Official list on PlayStation, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles; guide wording is original to this entry.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Whenever you acquire a vehicle you intend to keep — especially the distinct ones you are discovering anyway for Whip It Good — register it in the app at the time instead of batching the job later and forgetting which vehicles were never registered. Ten is a small target once the habit exists.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app for kept vehicles
Register each vehicle as you acquire it
